text:
maria: Heads-up — after last night's fleet push (driver 551.23 + CUDA 12.2) we're seeing a spike of kernel/linker failures on H100s in us-west-2. Errors look PTX/sm_90 related. Pods falling into CrashLoopBackOff on startup.
kevin: Can you paste the exact log? 
kevin: Also which AMI/image is this running?
sylvia: seeing similar in az-west-1 but much smaller. I put a small alert on the dashboard. :warning:
maria: log excerpt from one node: 
```
[2025-01-04 02:12:13] ptxas warning: Value 'sm_90' not supported by the linker
[2025-01-04 02:12:13] ptxas fatal   : Unresolved extern function _Z... in .v4b
cudaErrorSharedObjectSymbol: initialization error
```
maria: image is inference-runtime:v3.5 (we build kernels with -arch=sm_90 for H100 perf).
kevin: ok that looks like the JIT/ptx linker in the new driver choking on some object format. cc @ops-lead — any infra-level rolling back plan?
ops-lead: we have a rollback window, but need to be sure it's driver vs build flags. rolling a driver rollback to 545.x across the zone would be a 30–45m ops.
shawn: quick repro on a single machine: pulled the same image onto a fresh H100 with the new driver, ran a tiny kernel, got identical ptxas fatal. Rebooting didn't help.
sylvia: NCCL logs also have weird timeouts around the same time, but that could be downstream because the process never fully starts.
kevin: try setting CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY in the pod env to see if it defers JIT work (low risk). Also try forcing the runtime to use compiled cubin if present.
maria: I pushed a canary with CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY to one node, still crashlooping but different stack: "nvlink error: unresolved symbol".
ops-lead: Let's avoid big rollouts until we confirm. Options: (1) rollback driver cluster-wide, (2) rebuild the image with PTX -> cubin precompile targeting sm_90 with the new toolchain, (3) pin to older CUDA toolchain.
shawn: rebuilding might be safer for long-term. But rebuild + release will take ~2 hours and we need immediate mitigation for production.
kevin: For immediate mitigation, can we tag H100 nodes in us-west-2 as drained and fail traffic to other regions for a short window? Costy but safe.
ops-lead: doing a rolling drain of h100 pools in us-west-2 now. I'm leaving a small reserve for critical jobs. ETA 20m. :gear:
infra-bot: [autoscaler] evicted 24 pods from pool-h100-usw2 (drain initiated by ops-lead)
maria: we've set an alert rule to mute noisy errors to avoid paging on every PTX failure, but keep the aggregate error rate alert.
sylvia: I'll start a rebuild pipeline that emits both ptx and cubin artifacts and uploads them to the artifact store. If the new driver accepts precompiled cubins they should bypass the ptx linker.
kevin: note for postmortem: capture driver version, CUDA toolkit, nvcc flags, and nvcc/ptxas versions. Also check if any of the kernel object files include unsupported inline asm introduced by recent releases.
ops-lead: timeline so far: 02:12 first crash, 02:25 confirmed manifests, 02:32 started drain, 02:42 infra-bot evictions, 02:50 reduced traffic to h100 pools.
shawn: after rolling to fallback driver on one host (545.60) the same image runs fine. So this is definitely driver/toolchain incompat with our PTX.
maria: filing a bug with gpu-vendor; attaching logs and a minimal repro. Also adding a compatibility test to our preflight suite that runs on an H100 with the new driver before rollout.
kevin: good. For now keep H100 upgrades paused in all regions until the repro is addressed. We'll schedule a controlled flow for future upgrades with the preflight gate.
ops-lead: agreed. I'll also add a rollout policy: driver upgrades must hit a 3-node canary across 3 AZs and pass kernel sanity for 30m before wider rollout.
sylvia: PR for the rebuild pipeline is up, includes automated cubin generation and upload. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/ptx-repro/pull/12
maria: thanks team. Postmortem draft on me after we stabilize — include cost/impact estimates for the drain and failed runs.
kevin: thanks 🙏 keep updates here on the thread.
ops-lead: ongoing updates will be posted with timestamps; next update in ~15m."
